hyps.why: Stepping the learning rate up when it is already large causes divergence and big accuracy drops (e.g. experiments 7, 47).
Reducing an overly large learning rate rescues training (experiments 8, 10, 17, 18).
With very small learning rates, 243 epochs are undertrained, so raising it helps relative to when it is already large.
Strong L2 regularization underfits, so relaxing it helps (experiments 89, 90, 84).
Increasing an already large L2 penalty pushes the model into underfitting (experiments 83, 99).
Deeper nets are more prone to divergence at high learning rates (experiments 47, 55).
Removing a layer stabilizes training at high learning rates (experiments 48, 60, 56).
Wider networks have larger effective step sizes and diverge more readily at high learning rates (experiments 30, 39).
Going from one hidden layer to two adds capacity that helps more than going from two to three (experiments 54, 49, 50).
Very small batches are noisy and unstable with Adam, so a larger batch helps (experiments 69, 80).
